items: Confirm Before You Act, Item 1: Answer the three assessment questions honestly using only facts—not interpretations—what exactly was said, what exactly was your contribution, and did intent appear to be present.
Confirm Before You Act, Item 2: Complete the Credit Audit Worksheet in writing to separate what actually happened from what the situation means about your value as a professional.
Confirm Before You Act, Item 3: Identify one piece of work you know for certain was yours with no disputed attribution to use as your emotional anchor when doubt starts creeping in.
Confirm Before You Act, Item 4: Wait 24 hours before taking any action if you are uncertain whether theft actually occurred or if you are still emotionally charged from the incident.
Document Your Work, Item 1: Start a written record of each incident that includes the date, who was present, the exact words used, and what specific work was claimed as someone else's.
Document Your Work, Item 2: Preserve copies of your original work by saving emails, files, and version history that prove you created or contributed to the work being stolen.
Document Your Work, Item 3: Note all witnesses who observed your contribution in real time so you have corroboration available if you need to reference the incident later.
Document Your Work, Item 4: Track patterns over weeks or months instead of treating incidents as isolated events so you can identify whether this is a systematic problem with specific people.
Respond and Protect, Item 1: Speak directly to the person in a private conversation first using factual language rather than an accusatory tone before escalating to anyone else.
Respond and Protect, Item 2: Make your contributions publicly visible to decision-makers by sharing your work early in meetings and naturally tagging your involvement when appropriate.
Respond and Protect, Item 3: Ask clarifying questions in group settings without assigning blame when credit is being misattributed so others notice the omission themselves.
Respond and Protect, Item 4: Request written acknowledgment of your contribution from stakeholders involved so there is a documented trail protecting your work going forward.
